assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer and camera reframing for a 2D hand-drawn wasteland game background. Image 1 is the environment edit target. Image 2 is only the established character STYLE reference; never render its characters. Keep the thin ink, flat muted colors and old-paper/canvas material language, but correct the environmental scale for large full-body actors. The current environment reads as a distant wide panorama with miniature doors. REFRAME MUCH CLOSER at street level: nearby broken factory and plaster walls extend beyond the TOP and both SIDE edges. A human-scale loading doorway on the right must occupy about 53% of the complete canvas height, with its lintel around 13% image height and its base at 67%; do NOT draw small waist-high doors. Only a narrow gap of distant gray-olive ruins is visible between the nearby structures. Preserve a clear flat horizontal combat ground beginning at 67-69% height; this is where separate actors' feet will land. Actors separately composited at x=25% and 74% are about 43-48% of image height, so buildings and objects must make them look human-scale, not giants. Leave both standing locations unobstructed. Side-on theatrical battle camera, faint perspective only, no overhead or isometric view. Landscape 16:10 full bleed, production environment only. Sparse thin charcoal-brown linework, simple large flat shapes with one shadow tone, cool pale earth yellow / gray olive / ash gray / light brown, very restrained weathering, subtle matte paper texture. Neutral cloudy diffuse lighting; no orange/pink sunset, no bright sun disc, no rendered lighting, no pixel detail, no photorealism, no dense brick microtexture. Background strokes lighter and finer than the character strokes. Empty environment: no humans, creatures, UI, cards, text, logos, frames or contact shadows for absent actors. Output only this closer, correctly scaled environment.

Use case: style-transfer. Image 1 is the shelter-exterior environment to redraw. Image 2 is ONLY the exact art language reference for this game's existing characters. Redraw image 1 as a clean hand-drawn wasteland shelter exterior that can share a scene with those unchanged characters. Keep the shelter, patched canvas canopy, concrete loading area, open entrance, salvage crates and distant ruined town, but simplify the dense pixel detail into large deliberately drawn shapes. A scene background only: no people, creatures, UI, cards, lettering, logos or border. Thin charcoal-brown ink, outlines finer and lighter than the character outlines; flat cool earth-yellow, gray-olive, ash-gray and light-brown shapes; one restrained shadow tone per surface; very subtle matte paper texture, no blur. No pixel art, no photorealism, no detailed rendered rusty metal, no orange or pink sunset, no bright sun disc. Neutral diffuse cloudy daylight, with only a small subdued warm lamp inside the doorway. Landscape 16:10. Low side-on camera, human-scale entrance and crates; keep an unobstructed foreground standing position at x=25%, feet around 82% image height for an actor about 50% of frame height. The shelter should feel like the same material and drawing system as the poncho, bandages, backpack and work boots in image 2, not a different game. Quiet readable scene, more shape design and less texture noise. Output the empty environment only.

Redraw this same shelter interior as a sparse thin-ink hand-drawn wasteland scene. No glossy materials, no painterly blur, no 3D render. Camera low and close enough that the workbench and boxes feel human-scale: the front-right workbench is about a quarter of the canvas high from floor to tabletop. Empty foreground floor for a separately rendered full-body actor at x=25%, feet near 80% image height, height about 45-50% of frame. Keep this standing area clear of fire and furniture. Background only, landscape 16:10, full bleed. No people, creatures, cards, UI, lettering, logos or frames. Match the existing character costumes' muted sketch-and-flat-color language so they belong in the room without being repainted.
